content.title: UConn men have long history vs. UCLA coach Mick Cronin
content.text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - MARCH 20: Mick Cronin of the UCLA Bruins against the UCF Knights during the first half during the first round of the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament held at Xfinity Mobile Arena on March 20, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Ben Solomon/NCAA Photos via Getty Images)Ben Solomon/NCAA Photos via Getty ImagesPHILADELPHIA — On the surface, Dan Hurley and Mick Cronin share plenty of similarities.A couple of intense, follicly-challenged head coaches with Irish surnames and a tendency to ... well, complain about a thing or two. Both are sons of legendary high school coaches, both big Cincinnati Bengals fans. They've had their share of viral moments over the years, as well.Article continues below this adGet Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.ONLY 25¢That's on the surface, anyway. Peel back a bit and you've got Hurley, whose won a pair of national championships and is almost certainly heading to the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame, and Cronin, who has been to just one Final Four and had fans calling for his job when UCLA struggled out of the gates this season. The man ejected his own player from a game last month.Hurley and Cronin will meet for the first time in seven years on Sunday (8:45 p.m., TNT) when the second-seeded UConn men's basketball team faces No. 7 seed UCLA in an NCAA Tournament Round-of-32 bout at Xfinity Mobile Arena. The winner moves on to the East Regional semifinals later this week in Washington, D.C.More For YouPHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - MARCH 20: Mick Cronin of the UCLA Bruins against the UCF Knights during the second half during the first round of the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament held at Xfinity Mobile Arena on March 20, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Ben Solomon/NCAA Photos via Getty Images)Ben Solomon/NCAA Photos via Getty Images"I'm glad Hasheem Thabeet is not walking out there," Cronin said at a press conference on Saturday. "A lot of years in the same league. A lot of games with UConn. A lot of respect for them."Article continues below this adCT Insider LogoMake CT Insider a preferred source on Google to see more of our journalism when you search.Add Preferred SourceThat respect is mutual."Just the culture, the standards, how hard they play, the quality of shots they take, the discipline that they play with," Hurley said. "That never changes with a Mick Cronin team."On the surface, Cronin has gotten the better of the Huskies over the years. He was 15-11 against UConn over his 13-year career as Cincinnati's head coach, including seven straight wins from 2017-19. Article continues below this adAgain, that's just on the surface. A deeper dig reveals how UConn has been a massive thorn in the side of Cronin over the years, turning the diminutive head coach into somewhat of a punching bag. The Huskies have beaten and berated Cronin in so many different ways: from Jim Calhoun swiping Kemba Walker from under his nose, then falsely accusing him not voting Walker to the all-Big East team, to miracle comebacks and buzzer-beating shots — one of them a 75-footer!Here's a look at how the Huskies have stymied Cronin over the years:• June, 2007: Kemba Walker commits to UConn. When Cronin took over the reins at Cincinnati in March, 2006, he went in strong after Walker, and the two built up a strong relationship. “He did a great job recruiting me,” Walker said a few years later. “He had a great relationship with my parents.”Article continues below this adAlas, after Brandon Jennings elected not to go to UConn, Calhoun decided to go full bore on Walker, who still harbored UConn as his “dream school.” Two Final Fours, one national championship and a pair of broken Gary McGhee ankles later, the Huskies made out just fine.• Jan. 23, 2008: UConn trailed Cincinnati by 12 with just 5:52 left to play. Calhoun had incurred a costly technical, and it appeared the Huskies were headed towards a 3-4 start in Big East play.However, buoyed by some big shots from Jerome Dyson (who would be suspended from the team two days later), UConn made a furious comeback and left Fifth Third Arena with an improbable, 84-83 victory.• March 11, 2011: Walker makes the all-Big East First Team, but isn’t a unanimous selection. Only Notre Dame’s Ben Hansbrough is unanimously picked by the Big East coaches, and he wins player of the year honors.Article continues below this adCalhoun thinks he knows the one coach who didn’t vote for Kemba. You guessed it: Cronin.Seems Cronin had mentioned to the Cincinnati Enquirer a couple of weeks earlier how he nearly had Walker until Calhoun swooped in. Calhoun took that to mean Cronin was insanely jealous and still bitter at either Calhoun, Walker, or both, and didn’t vote for him.“My advice is, ‘Get over it,’” Calhoun said, without ever naming Cronin. “And don’t penalize the kid for the season he had. In the final analysis, in Kemba’s life ... he’ll probably have a longer career than that coach who didn’t vote for him.”Of course, Calhoun was purely speculating, and Cronin was peeved at Calhoun’s insinuation.Article continues below this ad“It’s not me (who didn’t vote for him), I can tell you that,” Cronin insisted. “If (Calhoun) wants to know who I voted for, he needs to ask me.”PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - MARCH 20: Head coach Mick Cronin of the UCLA Bruins yells out to his team against the UCF Knights in the first half during the first round of the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament at Xfinity Mobile Arena on March 20, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images)Mitchell Leff/Getty Images• March 18, 2011: Calhoun calls Cronin up and apologizes for his not-so-subtle jabs.The next day, UConn goes out and ends the Bearcats’ season, 69-58, in an NCAA tournament second-round game in Washington, D.C.Article continues below this adThe Huskies go on to win their third national championship.• March 1, 2014: Referee Ted Valentine gets up in Cronin’s grill after Cronin protested an out-of-bounds call at the XL Center. Valentine was out of line, as he’d later admit, and after the game, Cronin complained that he gets disrespected, and that refs wouldn’t get in Jim Boeheim’s or Coach K’s face.UConn wins the game, 51-45.• March 12, 2014: More conference player of the year controversy. Shabazz Napier earns the AAC award over Cincy’s Sean Kilpatrick. Kilpatrick’s not pleased, and neither is Cronin. After accepting the league coach of the year award, Cronin calls Kilpatrick “my player of the year” and never even mentions Napier. Upon leaving the ceremony, Cronin is overheard by reporters saying “Heroes are made in March, boys. This is all (expletive).”Article continues below this ad• March 14, 2014: Cronin, Kilpatrick and the Bearcats get their chance to avenge the player of the year “snub,” facing UConn in the league’s tournament semifinals. As always, it comes down to the final seconds. With 12 seconds left, Napier hits a free throw to put the Huskies up two, but uncharacteristically missed his second. Cincy came down and, of course, got the ball to Kilpatrick. He drove the lane, went up for the layup with a few ticks left on the clock and ... the ball rimmed in and out, fell to the floor, and UConn had the 58-56 victory.The Huskies would go on to win their fourth national championship.PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - MARCH 20: Head coach Mick Cronin of the UCLA Bruins reacts against the UCF Knights during the second half in the first round of the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament at Xfinity Mobile Arena on March 20, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images)Emilee Chinn/Getty Images• March 13, 2015: Unlike Kemba and Shabazz, Ryan Boatright had never had that defining, buzzer-beating clutch shot on his resume. Until this AAC tournament second-round bout with the Bearcats.Article continues below this adBoatright’s 3-pointer from the right wing rattled around the rim and sank through the net with 0.2 seconds remaining, giving the Huskies a 57-54 victory. (It should be pointed out: Cronin was not on the sidelines for this game. He missed most of the season while recovering from a medical scare that surely wasn’t helped if he watched the game on TV.)• March 11, 2016: Kevin Johnson buries a 3-pointer with 0.8 seconds left in the third overtime, and Cincy appears to have a victory in an AAC tourney quarterfinal bout that could send UConn to the NIT.But Jalen Adams collects the ensuing inbounds pass, takes a step and launches a 75-foot prayer. Somehow, it banks in, and the game heads to a fourth OT.There, UConn pulls away for a 104-97 victory. Cronin afterwards: “I felt we won the game and the game was taken away from us. In 0.8 seconds, you can’t catch the ball, take two steps and then shoot it … The clock didn’t start nearly on time.”Article continues below this adThe win jump-starts UConn to its first AAC tourney title.Cronin is still peeved about it to this day."No chance that was good," he said on Saturday. "At the end of the day, it didn't matter. Conference tournaments are to line people's pockets."Article continues below this adNow, to be fair, Cronin has gotten the better of the Huskies a few times, as well. The Bearcats ended UConn's hopes for a miracle run in the 2017 American Athletic Conference tournament in Hartford with an 81-71 victory in the championship game. On Feb. 24, 2019, in Hurley's first year at UConn's helm, Cincy notched a 64-60 win in Hartford that included a 30-footer at the shot-clock buzzer with just 12 seconds left. To add insult to injury, the shot was by Cane Broome, an East Hartford product.That marked the last time Cronin has faced the Huskies. The following year, he left Cincinnati for UCLA, where he's yet to play UConn. That ends late Sunday night, where Cronin can either add to his short list of key victories over the Huskies ... or add to his much longer list of excruciating losses.CT Insider LogoGet daily updates from the UConn basketball world.March 21, 2026|Updated March 21, 2026 5:31 p.m.Staff WriterDave Borges is a sports reporter for Hearst Connecticut Media Group covering the UConn men's basketball team. An award-winning journalist, Dave has covered the Huskies since 2007, including coverage of five Final Fours and four national championships (2011, 2014, 2023 and 2024). He has been an Associated Press Top 25 poll voter since 2009 and was named NSMA Connecticut Sportswriter of the Year in 2019. Dave has authored three books: "Hurley's Heroes: UConn's Return to College Basketball's Elite," "Rebound: The Incredible Story of UConn Basketball's Comeback from Defeat to Dominance," and "Images of Baseball: The Pawtucket Red Sox." He also covers baseball and was a beat writer chronicling the 2004 World Series-champion Boston Red Sox. Dave has been a Baseball Hall of Fame voter since 2014. He can be reached at david.borges@hearstmediact.com.
